title: The Waratah
subtitle: SS Waratah · off South Africa, 1909
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the open sea off the southeast coast of South Africa in July 1909, early-1900s steamship era, grey-green water and heavy southern-winter sky, cold steel-grey light, melancholy and uncanny, period maritime detail, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: South Africa, July nineteen-oh-nine. The Waratah, a big new liner, left Durban for Cape Town. She never arrived.
beats.img: A large early-1900s steamship with a single tall funnel and two masts, black hull and white upper decks, sailing alone on a grey-green open sea in clear daylight, seen broadside and centred in frame, sharp and well lit, a faint trail of smoke from the funnel, no people.

beats.vo: Two hundred and eleven people were aboard. None was ever seen again.
beats.img: The empty promenade deck of an early-1900s steamship in daylight, polished wooden deck planks, white-painted railings and a row of empty wooden deck chairs, lifeboats in their davits above, grey sea beyond, still and deserted, no people.

beats.vo: Early the next morning, another steamer exchanged lamp signals with her. It was the last confirmed sighting.
beats.img: A brass signal lamp shining a bright beam from the dark bridge wing of an early-1900s cargo steamer before dawn, across a heaving sea toward the small distant lights of a larger steamship on the horizon, cold blue pre-dawn light, no people.

beats.vo: One passenger left the ship at Durban. He later cabled his wife that he had thought her top-heavy.
beats.img: A large early-1900s steamship with a single tall funnel moored alongside a quiet stone harbour quay in soft daylight, a lone leather suitcase resting on the empty quay in the foreground, coiled mooring ropes, calm water, no people.

beats.vo: For decades, searchers combed that coast. One promising wreck turned out to be another ship. The Waratah has never been found.
beats.img: A wide empty grey ocean off a rugged dark coastline under a heavy overcast sky, long swells rolling toward the horizon, no ship anywhere, cold and unresolved.

facts.claim: SS Waratah, Blue Anchor Line passenger-cargo liner (~9,339 GRT), completed October 1908, maiden voyage November 1908; lost on her second voyage, July 1909
Left Durban on the evening of 26 July 1909 bound for Cape Town (due 29 July); never arrived
211 people aboard (92 passengers, 119 crew); none ever seen or heard from again. Figure consistent across sources checked
Early on 27 July 1909 the steamer Clan MacIntyre exchanged signal-lamp messages with Waratah off the Eastern Cape (near the Mbashe River); the last confirmed sighting
Passenger Claude Sawyer disembarked at Durban and cabled his wife 'Thought Waratah top-heavy, landed Durban' (his later reported vision/dream is anecdote and is NOT used)
Emlyn Brown's searches 1983-2004; a 1999 sonar target that seemed to match was identified by divers in 2001 as the Nailsea Meadow, a WWII wreck; Brown gave up in 2004
Still not found as of 2025-26: a 2025 Journal of Maritime Archaeology paper (rogue-wave hypothesis, Algoa Bay shelf break) states the ship remains undiscovered despite many searches
